title: Physical Backups & Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR)
description: Archive Write-Ahead Logs (WAL) continuously and restore the database to the exact second before a disaster occurred.

data.text: While logical backups (`pg_dump`) export SQL commands, enterprise disaster recovery relies on **Continuous Archiving and Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR)**. By combining a base physical backup (`pg_basebackup`) with a stream of archived WAL segments, you can restore your database to any exact timestamp.

data.caption: Point-In-Time Recovery Mechanism
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Base Backup: Sunday 00:00] --> B[WAL Stream: Sun - Wed]
    B --> C{Accidental DROP TABLE: Wed 14:15:00}
    A --> D[Replay WAL to Target]
    B --> D
    D -->|recovery_target_time = 14:14:59| E[Clean Database Restored Without Data Loss]

data.text: The Base Backup and Recovery Target

PITR is a base backup plus every WAL segment generated after it. To recover, you restore the base backup, place the archived WAL where the server can read it, set a recovery target, and start. PostgreSQL replays WAL forward until it reaches the target, then promotes.

data.title: Take a base backup and restore to a point in time
data.content: `-Ft` produces a tar archive with the WAL needed for consistency; the restore replays archived segments up to the moment before the accident.
data.code:
# Take the base backup (run in a directory outside the data dir)
pg_basebackup \
  -D /backup/base-$(date +%F) \
  -Ft -z -P \
  -X stream

# --- Later: recover to just before the accidental DROP ---
# 1. Extract the base backup into the data directory
# 2. Write recovery settings into postgresql.auto.conf
cat >> $PGDATA/postgresql.auto.conf <<'EOF'
restore_command = 'cp /wal_archive/%f %p'
recovery_target_time = '2024-05-01 14:14:00+00'
recovery_target_action = 'promote'
EOF

touch $PGDATA/recovery.signal
pg_ctl start

data.title: Test the restore, not just the backup
data.text: A backup that has never been restored is an assumption. Restore into a scratch instance periodically, confirm the data and the recovery target, and time the whole process — that measured time is your real RTO, which is usually far larger than the estimate. Automated tools such as pgBackRest, WAL-G, and Barman wrap this workflow and add retention, compression, and verification for you.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PITR combines a physical base backup with continuous WAL segment archiving.
Allows rolling back to the exact second prior to accidental data loss.
Tools like `pgBackRest` and `WAL-G` automate enterprise PITR to S3/GCS.
